# Exact fixed-batch categorical coupling

This is the finite-alphabet fixed-batch premise inherited from Astra N1691, stated and proved here so the hard-cap comparison can be read without another archive. It is not a new claim of this package.

## 1. Setup

There are r>=1 independent P records, the first being the actual supplied X, and s>=1 independent Q records. The positive integers r,s are fixed before sampling. An algorithm may use all ordered records and independent auxiliary randomness. It must output Y with exactly law Q for every pair P,Q. It cannot query further source records or use the unknown probabilities.

Let A=(A_1,...,A_d) and B=(B_1,...,B_d) be the two count vectors. Conditional on A=a,B=b, all compatible ordered P lists are equiprobable, and likewise for Q lists. The conditional distribution of the records therefore does not depend on P,Q. In particular

    Pr(X=j | A=a,B=b)=a_j/r.

Write g_j(a,b)=Pr(Y=j | A=a,B=b), averaging the algorithm's auxiliary randomness and all compatible ordered lists.

## 2. Universal exactness forces the empirical target marginal

For every P,Q in the interiors of their simplexes, universal exactness says

    sum_(a,b) Mult_r(a) Mult_s(b) P^a Q^b g_j(a,b) = q_j,

where |a|=r, |b|=s and Mult_r(a)=r!/(product_i a_i!). The homogeneous Bernstein representation of q_j at degrees (r,s) is

    q_j = sum_(a,b) Mult_r(a) Mult_s(b) P^a Q^b (b_j/s).

For completeness, this representation is unique. If the difference vanishes on the product of simplexes, homogeneity makes it vanish on every pair of strictly positive vectors: scale each vector by its coordinate sum and multiply by the corresponding sum to powers r and s. A polynomial zero on this open set has every monomial coefficient zero. Thus

    g_j(a,b)=b_j/s

for every pair of count vectors. Boundary distributions follow by the same polynomial identity or by continuity. No assumption about a preferred ordering, linear algorithm or deterministic decision rule was used.

## 3. Optimal disagreement and a matching operation

Conditional on the count vectors, (X,Y) is a coupling of a/r and b/s. Therefore

    Pr(X != Y | A=a,B=b) >= TV(a/r,b/s).

A maximal categorical coupling of those empirical histograms attains equality while retaining the actual X as its first coordinate. Let

    R=1-sum_i h_i.

# All fixed per-source batch allocations

This separate analytic strengthening concerns the exact empirical-coupling comparator in N1691. It is not a lower bound for arbitrary adaptive stopping rules. Let d>=2 and let r>=1 P records (including the supplied X) and s>=1 Q records be fixed in advance. The new-call budget is r+s-1. Under the N1691 fixed-batch characterization, no alternate processing of these same records has smaller expected disagreement than their empirical total variation.

For P=Q uniform on d labels, put

    t=r+s, u=rs, k=(d-1)/d^2,
    D=Bin(r,1/d)/r - Bin(s,1/d)/s,

where the binomials are independent. Then the optimal disagreement is delta=d E|D|/2. Independent centered Bernoulli moments give

    v=E D^2=k t/u,
    E D^4=3v^2+k(1-6k)(r^(-3)+s^(-3))
          <=3v^2+k(r^(-3)+s^(-3)).

Holder interpolation yields E|D|>=v^(3/2)/(E D^4)^(1/2). Since (r^(-3)+s^(-3))/(r^(-1)+s^(-1))=(t^2-3u)/u^2, this becomes

    delta >= d k t/[2 sqrt(t^2+3u(kt-1))].

If kt>=1, use u<=t^2/4 to obtain

    delta >= [(d-1)/d]/sqrt(1+3kt).

If kt<1, the denominator in the preceding expression is at most 2t, hence delta>=(d-1)/(2d). Thus for any target eta<(d-1)/(2d), delta<=eta necessarily implies

    t >= (d-1)/(3 eta^2) - d^2/[3(d-1)].

At d=16 and eta=1/100, this is t>=49,994+14/45, so the integer total-record count is at least 49,995 and there are at least 49,994 NEW draws. For balanced r=s, t is even, and at least 49,995 new draws are required. These are lower bounds, not claimed exact optimal counts.

The proposed adaptive factory's uniform guarantee at L=100 remains 3,169 expected new calls. This strengthens the comparison from balanced fixed batches to every fixed per-source allocation; it still compares an expected stopping budget to a deterministic fixed-batch budget. It does not exclude a better adaptive categorical construction, establish minimax optimality, or compare actual runtime.

No experiment or numerical calculation has been run to obtain these bounds.

# Hard-cap and second-moment lower bounds

9 November 2026. Mathematical proof export. These two arguments were independently derived and checked. The source binding is recorded in PROVENANCE.json; exposition and cross-references have been adapted for this self-contained package. No execution or runtime measurement is asserted.

## Two preliminary boundaries

The original factory has no distribution-uniform second-moment bound. For L>=2 and P=Q, its first stage conditional on X=i has mean (L-1)/p_i. Conditional Jensen therefore gives

    E N_first^2 >= (L-1)^2 sum_(i:p_i>0) 1/p_i.

This diverges as one atom tends to zero even with fixed d=2. It is a defect of that original factory, not an impossibility for all algorithms; the local-cap construction repairs it.

Universal exact maximality is impossible in the finite-transcript sample-only model. At an equal full-support pair P=Q, a maximal coupling must never disagree. Every finite sample-word transcript that can occur at another full-support pair has positive likelihood at this equal pair. The independent auxiliary randomness has the same law. Thus a terminal disagreeing event of positive probability at another full-support pair would also have positive probability at equality. Formally, restrict to each finite query count and source/sample-word sequence and use mutual absolute continuity, then take the countable union. No such event is possible, so the algorithm would always retain X even for unequal full-support P,Q, contradicting the exact Q marginal. This explains the need for positive slack but does not determine its cost.

## 1. Hard-cap obstruction extends to adaptive source allocation

Consider any universally exact sample-only coupling procedure that uses at most M fresh oracle calls on every run. Its requests may adaptively alternate between P and Q and depend on all previous observations. Pre-generate M independent fresh P records and M independent Q records, and answer each requested call from the next unused record of its requested source. This exactly simulates the procedure. Including supplied X, it is processing a fixed collection of r=M+1 P records and s=M Q records; unused records are simply ignored.
